candidates.name: Lab-accreditation scope schedules that list each lab's sequencers, with dated issue numbers (UKAS ISO 15189 and 17025 in the UK, DAkkS in Germany, INAB in Ireland, SAS in Switzerland)
candidates.access: Download the public UKAS schedule PDFs at https://www.ukas.com/download-schedule/{accreditation_no}/Medical or /Testing. Confirmed numbers: 8523 is Illumina Laboratory Services (PDF metadata 11 Sep 2026; a copy is already saved at C:\Users\palaz\.claude\projects\C--Users-palaz-OneDrive-Documents-ILMN-Claude-Code-Local-Folder--Build-thesis-scrape-sandbox\72ecacdd-e343-417c-86d9-625b7cbb4ed0\tool-results\webfetch-1791792585438-y5nbsf.pdf). 8993 is Cooper Genomics, 8727 is UKHSA Colindale, and 20372 is Novogene UK (17025; its snippet names the NovaSeq 6000). Also try 29022 and 29671. The PDFs use FlateDecode compression, so extract the text locally with `python -I` and pypdf. For the German and Irish schedules use https://dakks.de/files/data/as/pdf/D-PL-xxxxx-xx-xx.pdf (for example D-PL-13374-01-01, D-PL-17038-01-00 and D-PL-21662-01-00, and DKFZ D-PL-20890-03-00) and https://inab.ie/fileupload/medical-testing/genseq-diagnostics-421mt.pdf. For more, search Google with: site:ukas.com/download-schedule "NovaSeq", site:dakks.de "NovaSeq", and site:inab.ie "NovaSeq". The South West GLH page (nbt.nhs.uk/south-west-genomic-laboratory-hub/virtual-advisorfaqs) says its X Plus is 'unaccredited, pending assessment'.
candidates.rationale: Accredited clinical labs must list their equipment in the scope. A 6000 that is still on the 2026 schedule while the X is missing or 'pending assessment' is hard evidence that validated clinical assays keep the 6000 tail alive. Comparing successive issue numbers dates when each lab adds the X and when it drops the 6000. The result is a rare, dated census of who still runs clinical work on the 6000 outside the US (NHS GLHs, German Institute labs, private clinical labs) and how slow the regulatory switch is. That speaks directly to whether the tail is 'permanent' or keeps converting, and to the 2027 conversion pace.

candidates.name: EMQN/GenQA NGS external quality assessment (EQA) summary reports: the sequencer platforms participating clinical labs report, year over year
candidates.access: The 2025 germline report (dated 30 Apr 2026) is already saved locally at ...\tool-results\webfetch-1791792576589-rm301c.pdf. Extract its text with `python -I` and pypdf and look for the 'platform', 'instrument' or 'sequencer' tables in the results section and appendices. Then pull the earlier rounds for a time series: the somatic 2024 report at https://www.emqn.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/NGS-Somatic-EQA-Summary-report-2024-v1.pdf, and older reports via https://www.emqn.org/resources/publications/ and Google site:emqn.org/wp-content/uploads "Summary Report" NGS. Euformatics (eqa.euformatics.com) runs a bioinformatics EQA that tracks results by instrument.
candidates.rationale: EQA schemes collect the platform each participating diagnostic lab uses, often across a few hundred mostly European clinical labs. A 2023→2024→2025 series of shares (NovaSeq 6000 vs X vs NextSeq vs MGI/Element) would directly measure how fast clinical labs are converting and how large the 6000 holdout remains. These figures would be independent of Illumina's own disclosures, which stopped after Q4'25. It is unverified whether the reports include a platform table, because the text did not render.

candidates.name: NCBI Genetic Testing Registry (GTR): the instrument named in each clinical test's methodology field (NovaSeq 6000 vs NovaSeq X), with lab names and record update dates
candidates.access: Use the free NCBI E-utilities API (no login). Run esearch https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?db=gtr&term=%22NovaSeq%206000%22&retmax=5000, then the same with %22NovaSeq%20X%22, %22NextSeq%22, %22AVITI%22, %22DNBSEQ%22 and %22Ultima%22. Then call esummary or efetch (db=gtr) on the IDs to get the lab name, test type and last-update date. The GTR bulk FTP (ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/GTR/data/test_version.gz) carries version history, so you can catch records whose instrument changed from 6000 to X. Test 560898 is a confirmed example: a whole-transcriptome RNA-seq test that lists the NovaSeq 6000 as its instrument.
candidates.rationale: US CLIA labs register thousands of tests in GTR with an instrument field. Counting live 6000 tests by lab (reference labs, academic hospitals, hereditary and oncology labs) and by test type shows who the remaining clinical 6000 users are. Records updated in 2025–26 that still say 6000 point to tests where revalidation hasn't happened. Version history that shows 6000→X switches gives a conversion rate. Low-volume, many-assay labs on the 6000 would support the low-elasticity cohort (Thaysen's cohort 1/2).

The quantity and price lines on 6000 reagent buys vs X kit buys show whether these holdouts react to price at all. A 1-year 'Bronze' service renewal tells you the planned remaining life. The NHGRI $90M ceiling at 1% use also hints at research purchasing pace.

candidates.name: Canadian provincial health-authority direct-award notices for NovaSeq 6000 and X consumables (BC PHSA, plus Ontario, Alberta and Québec health agencies)
candidates.access: Open the BCPHSA notice (notice of intent to direct-award NovaSeq 6000 and X Plus consumables, 2023) and record its term, value, and the 6000 vs X line items. Then search CanadaBuys for 'NovaSeq' with a 2025–26 date filter, and search BC Bid, Alberta Purchasing Connection and Ontario Tenders Portal (or Google site:canadabuys.canada.ca "NovaSeq" and site:bcbid.gov.bc.ca "Illumina"). This differs from S207, the Element benchtop award, and from S457, the federal proactive disclosure.
candidates.rationale: Provincial public-health and clinical genetics labs, such as BCCDC and provincial hereditary-cancer labs, are classic regulated 6000 holdouts. Direct-award renewals that still split 6000 and X consumables in 2025–26, with multi-year terms, are documented proof that the tail persists. Where values and quantities are given, changes in the 6000 volume share between successive notices measure the conversion pace and whether price moved it.

candidates.access: Open the Roswell Park June 2026 agenda PDF and read the 'Illumina Next Generation Sequencing' contract or capital item: amount, term, and whether it covers 6000 reagents or an X. Do the same for the later Roswell Park agendas (Sep 2026) and the U. Illinois trustees' 'purchases and renewals' docx series (trustees.uillinois.edu/trustees/agenda/; the 2023 item was an X Plus at the Carver Center). Also run Google searches: "board" "agenda" "Illumina" "NovaSeq 6000" (2026, filetype:pdf), and "capital budget" "NovaSeq" FY2027 hospital.
candidates.rationale: Public hospital boards must approve sole-source Illumina contracts with dollar amounts and terms. A FY27 capital line that replaces a 6000, or a multi-year renewal of 6000 reagents and service, dates when (or whether) clinical holdouts convert. Contract language about pricing tiers or discounts would support the extra-discount thesis.

candidates.name: University and hospital shared-instrumentation funding notices that justify replacing a NovaSeq 6000 with an X (UW–Madison research office and equivalents), 2025–26
candidates.access: Open the UW–Madison page 'Replacement of an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 with a NovaSeq X Plus' and extract the date, cost, funding source, the 6000's age and service cost, and the stated reasons (cost per Gb vs end-of-service). Then search Google for: "replacement of" "NovaSeq 6000" site:.edu, "NovaSeq 6000" "end of service" OR "service contract" 2026 site:.edu, and "NovaSeq 6000" "will be retired" 2026.
candidates.rationale: Internal funding requests spell out why a lab is leaving the 6000 (rising service contracts, cost per Gb, Illumina support timelines) or can't afford to. Whether each driver is price or end of life tells you if 6000 users respond to price, or wait for support to lapse, which would mean a slower tail. These pages are mostly research labs, so they cover the residual ~8% of research Gb still on the 6000.
